name: Agentic Enterprise
summary: Companies deploy agents for support, sales, finance and HR and standardize on MCP. Revenue and valuations are rising, but many pilots show no clear return and agent security is unresolved.

regions.name: Customer support agents
regions.summary: The most deployed enterprise agent use case. Sierra and Decagon reach multi-billion valuations and pricing shifts to per resolution, while some early adopters bring humans back.

landmarks.name: Sierra raises $950M at over $15B
landmarks.summary: Bret Taylor's customer experience agent company raised $950M led by Tiger Global and GV, taking its post-money valuation above $15B.

landmarks.name: Decagon $250M at $4.5B
landmarks.summary: Support agent startup raised a Series D led by Coatue and Index Ventures, saying it tripled its valuation in under six months.

landmarks.name: Klarna brings human agents back
landmarks.summary: A year after saying its AI assistant did the work of 700 agents, Klarna's CEO said the cost focus had lowered quality and the firm began recruiting human support staff again.

regions.whyItMatters: Support is where agents first replaced human work at scale, so it shows early what works and what quality costs follow.
regions.openQuestion: How much support can agents fully resolve before quality and customer trust suffer?

deepDives.title: τ-bench leaderboards
deepDives.why: Scores for agents handling simulated support conversations under policy rules, in text and voice.

deepDives.title: Generative AI at Work (Brynjolfsson, Li, Raymond)
deepDives.why: Field study of 5,172 support agents: AI assistance raised issues resolved per hour by 15% on average.

deepDives.title: CX Today: HubSpot Bets Big on Outcome-Based AI Pricing
deepDives.why: How Zendesk, Salesforce and HubSpot are moving from seats to pay-per-resolution pricing.

regions.name: Sales & marketing
regions.summary: CRM vendors sell agents for prospecting, outreach and service, some priced per outcome. Agentforce passed $1B ARR but is still small next to Salesforce's core business.

landmarks.name: Agentforce ARR reaches $800M
landmarks.summary: Salesforce reported Agentforce ARR of $800M, up 169% year on year, and over 29,000 deals closed since launch, in fiscal 2026 fourth quarter results.

landmarks.name: Agentforce ARR reaches $1.2B
landmarks.summary: Salesforce's first quarter fiscal 2027 results put Agentforce ARR at $1.2B, up 205% year on year, against quarterly revenue of $11.1B.

landmarks.name: HubSpot prices agents per outcome
landmarks.summary: From 14 April HubSpot charges $1 per lead its Prospecting Agent recommends for outreach and $0.50 per conversation its Customer Agent resolves.

regions.whyItMatters: CRM vendors are the test of whether agents add revenue to incumbent software or only replace seat licences.
regions.openQuestion: Will per-outcome pricing replace per-seat licences, and who decides what counts as an outcome?

deepDives.title: Bessemer: The AI pricing and monetization playbook
deepDives.why: Primer on consumption, workflow and outcome-based pricing models for AI products.

deepDives.title: MarTech: HubSpot moves to outcome-based pricing for some Breeze AI agents
deepDives.why: Independent trade coverage of what outcome pricing changes for marketing and sales teams.

deepDives.title: Salesforce: Record First Quarter Fiscal 2027 Results
deepDives.why: Primary numbers on Agentforce and Data 360 ARR relative to total Salesforce revenue.

regions.name: Finance & back office
regions.summary: ERP and accounting vendors embed agents for accruals, reconciliations and month-end close, with humans keeping sign-off. Many features are still in pilot or restricted release.

landmarks.name: SAP Accounting Accruals Agent
landmarks.summary: Joule agent that reads accrual policies, pulls history and drafts journal entries for accountants to review, released in restricted availability.

landmarks.name: Intuit Agentic Books Close
landmarks.summary: At Intuit Connect, Intuit announced agents that work through a firm's monthly close steps for review. It is in pilot with a limited group of firms.

landmarks.name: Intuit four mid-market finance agents
landmarks.summary: Intuit launched finance, payments, accounting and project management agents in Intuit Enterprise Suite, its mid-market product.

regions.whyItMatters: Finance needs audit trails and sign-off, so it tests whether agents can work under strict controls.
regions.openQuestion: Will auditors and CFOs accept agent-prepared entries without line-by-line human review?

deepDives.title: SAPinsider: SAP's Autonomous Finance push and the governance picture
deepDives.why: How finance agents fit with audit evidence, controls and accountability in SAP estates.

deepDives.title: Futurum: Intuit Intelligence Positions Accountants as Intuit's ERP Channel
deepDives.why: Analyst view on which Intuit agent features are live versus pilot or coming soon.

deepDives.title: ICAEW: Artificial intelligence resources
deepDives.why: Accountancy body's hub of guidance and case studies on AI and agents in finance and audit.

deepDives.title: FinanceBench: A New Benchmark for Financial Question Answering
deepDives.why: Benchmark paper testing how reliably language models answer questions on company filings.

regions.name: HR & recruiting
regions.summary: Agents source candidates, run screening chats and schedule interviews at scale. Bias litigation against AI screening is testing vendor liability.

landmarks.name: Workday completes Paradox acquisition
landmarks.summary: Workday closed its purchase of the conversational hiring agent maker, pairing it with Workday Recruiting and HiredScore.

landmarks.name: Mobley v. Workday advances
landmarks.summary: Judge Rita Lin let California fair employment claims proceed while dismissing some others, after a May 2025 collective certification on age claims.

landmarks.name: Juicebox $80M Series B
landmarks.summary: AI recruiting search platform raised a round led by DST Global at an $850M valuation and says more than 5,000 recruiting teams use it.

regions.whyItMatters: Hiring is a high-stakes use of agents where discrimination law applies directly to automated decisions.
regions.openQuestion: Is the vendor or the employer liable when an AI screening tool discriminates?

deepDives.title: Akin AI law tracker: Mobley v. Workday
deepDives.why: Entry in a running tracker of AI law and regulation, with the case background.

deepDives.title: Fisher Phillips: Workday AI hiring suit can proceed as class action
deepDives.why: Plain-language employer guide to the May 2025 collective certification ruling.

deepDives.title: Gender, Race, and Intersectional Bias in Resume Screening via Language Model Retrieval
deepDives.why: Study finding text embedding models favored White-associated names in 85% of resume screening tests.

deepDives.title: Duane Morris Class Action Weekly Wire: Mobley v. Workday ruling
deepDives.why: Regular legal commentary and podcast on algorithmic bias class actions.

regions.name: Enterprise search & knowledge work
regions.summary: Work assistants search across company apps and run prebuilt agents. Glean grows quickly on usage-based revenue while Microsoft bundles Copilot and agent management into a top-tier suite.

landmarks.name: Glean passes $300M ARR
landmarks.summary: Enterprise search and agent vendor says it tripled ARR in 15 months. TechCrunch notes part of it is consumption-based, so not strictly recurring.

landmarks.name: Microsoft 365 E7 and Agent 365 ship
landmarks.summary: Microsoft made Agent 365, a control plane for agents, generally available at $15 per user a month, alongside the E7 suite bundling it with Copilot at $99.

landmarks.name: Glean valued at $7.2B
landmarks.summary: Glean raised a $150M Series F led by Wellington Management, valuing the enterprise search company at $7.2B.

regions.whyItMatters: Whoever holds company context across apps is positioned to become the default front end for work agents.
regions.openQuestion: Will a neutral layer like Glean hold against assistants bundled into Microsoft and Google suites?

deepDives.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey
deepDives.why: Survey of the retrieval techniques that enterprise search assistants are built on.

deepDives.title: Microsoft Agent 365 documentation
deepDives.why: Reference for how one suite vendor registers, permissions and monitors enterprise agents.

deepDives.title: Microsoft Work Trend Index
deepDives.why: Annual survey and telemetry research on how AI and agents are changing knowledge work.

deepDives.title: TechCrunch: Glean's top line crosses $300M
deepDives.why: Explains consumption revenue and the token-cost argument for a neutral context layer.

regions.name: Agent platforms & protocols (MCP, A2A)
regions.summary: MCP is the default way to connect agents to tools, now under neutral foundation governance alongside A2A. Labs and suite vendors compete to be the enterprise agent platform.

landmarks.name: Agentic AI Foundation formed
landmarks.summary: Linux Foundation body launched with Anthropic's MCP, Block's goose and OpenAI's AGENTS.md as founding projects.

landmarks.name: OpenAI Frontier
landmarks.summary: Enterprise platform to run agents as digital coworkers, including third-party ones, with HP, Intuit, Oracle and Uber among early customers.

landmarks.name: A2A joins the AAIF
landmarks.summary: Google's agent-to-agent protocol, at the Linux Foundation since 2025, was accepted as a growth stage project at the AAIF, the same home as MCP.

regions.whyItMatters: Shared protocols decide whether enterprise agents interoperate or stay locked into one vendor's platform.
regions.openQuestion: Will open protocols keep agent platforms interoperable, or will a few vendors control the layer?

deepDives.title: Model Context Protocol documentation
deepDives.why: Specification and documentation for the protocol connecting models to tools.

deepDives.title: A2A Protocol documentation
deepDives.why: Official specification, SDKs and tutorials for agent-to-agent communication.

deepDives.title: Agentic AI Foundation
deepDives.why: Home of the foundation governing MCP, A2A, goose and AGENTS.md, with projects and members.

deepDives.title: A survey of agent interoperability protocols: MCP, ACP, A2A and ANP
deepDives.why: Compares the main agent protocols and where each fits in a deployment.

regions.name: Agent governance, identity & security
regions.summary: Identity vendors and NIST are defining how agents get credentials and owners, while prompt injection has caused demonstrated data leaks on major agent platforms.

landmarks.name: Okta Agent SSO generally available
landmarks.summary: Okta added agent identities with short-lived tokens to core SSO, built on Cross App Access, which is now an MCP authorization extension.

landmarks.name: NIST AI Agent Standards Initiative
landmarks.summary: NIST's CAISI launched work on agent interoperability, security and identity, with a request for information and an identity concept paper.

landmarks.name: Copilot Studio and Agentforce data leaks
landmarks.summary: Capsule Security showed that text in public forms could make Copilot Studio and Agentforce agents leak corporate data. Both vendors issued patches.

regions.whyItMatters: Agents act with real credentials, so unsolved prompt injection turns ordinary inputs like web forms into attack paths.
regions.openQuestion: Can prompt injection be contained well enough for agents to act on untrusted input with real permissions?

deepDives.title: NIST Agent Standards Initiative hub
deepDives.why: Official hub for NIST's agent security, identity and interoperability work as it appears.

deepDives.title: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications for 2026
deepDives.why: Community-reviewed list of the main security risks for agentic applications.

deepDives.title: Design Patterns for Securing LLM Agents against Prompt Injections
deepDives.why: Proposes agent designs that limit what injected text can make an agent do.

deepDives.title: Simon Willison on prompt injection
deepDives.why: Running commentary on the attack class behind most agent security incidents.

regions.name: Computer-use & browser agents
regions.summary: Agents that click through websites and desktops are improving but still fail most long tasks. OpenAI retired its standalone browser and moved agent features into its desktop app and extensions.

landmarks.name: ChatGPT Atlas launched
landmarks.summary: OpenAI released an AI browser for macOS with a preview agent mode that takes actions on web pages, challenging Chrome.

landmarks.name: OpenAI retires Atlas
landmarks.summary: OpenAI said Atlas would stop working on 9 August, about ten months after launch, folding browsing into its ChatGPT desktop app and Chrome extensions.

landmarks.name: OSWorld 2.0 long-horizon results
landmarks.summary: A harder computer-use benchmark of 108 long tasks found the top setup, Claude Opus 4.8, fully completed 20.6% of tasks with a 54.8% partial score.

regions.whyItMatters: Computer use lets agents work in software that has no API, which is most enterprise software.
regions.openQuestion: When will computer-use agents finish long multi-step tasks reliably enough to run unattended?

deepDives.title: Epoch AI: OSWorld 2.0
deepDives.why: Tracked model scores on long-horizon computer-use tasks over time.

deepDives.title: OSWorld 2.0: Benchmarking Computer Use Agents on Long-Horizon Real-World Tasks
deepDives.why: Benchmark design and the failure modes agents show on tasks that take people over an hour.

deepDives.title: OSWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents in Real Computer Environments
deepDives.why: The original 369-task benchmark that became the standard measure for computer-use agents.

deepDives.title: WebArena: A Realistic Web Environment for Building Autonomous Agents
deepDives.why: Widely used benchmark of web tasks on self-hosted sites, with a human baseline.

regions.name: Adoption, ROI & failure rates
regions.summary: Spending keeps rising, but studies and analysts report most pilots never reach measurable return and that AI-linked job cuts do not track ROI, fueling debate over agent hype.

landmarks.name: MIT NANDA: 95% see no return on GenAI
landmarks.summary: The GenAI Divide report, based on 52 interviews and a 153-person survey, said 95% of organizations had seen zero return from generative AI efforts.

landmarks.name: Gartner: 40% of agent projects to be cut
landmarks.summary: Gartner predicted over 40% of agentic AI projects will be canceled by end of 2027 and said only about 130 vendors offer real agentic products.

landmarks.name: Gartner: half of AI service cuts reversed
landmarks.summary: Gartner predicted that by 2027 half of companies that cut customer service staff because of AI will rehire for similar work under new titles.

landmarks.name: Gartner: job cuts not linked to AI ROI
landmarks.summary: A Gartner survey of 350 executives at large firms reportedly found about 80% had cut headcount, with no correlation to higher returns on AI.

regions.whyItMatters: Valuations and budgets assume agents pay off, and the evidence so far is mixed and often vendor-supplied.
regions.openQuestion: Is weak measured ROI a deployment lag that will close, or a sign that agent value is overstated?

deepDives.title: Stanford HAI: AI Index
deepDives.why: Annual independent data report on AI capability, investment and business adoption.

deepDives.title: The Anthropic Economic Index
deepDives.why: Recurring data on which work tasks people and firms use one lab's models for.

deepDives.title: McKinsey: The state of AI
deepDives.why: Long-running global survey of how organizations use AI and whether they report value.

deepDives.title: People Matters: 55% of employers regret AI layoffs
deepDives.why: Pulls together Forrester, Gartner and other findings on AI layoffs and rehiring.

deepDives.title: Model Context Protocol documentation
deepDives.why: Specification for the protocol most enterprise agents use to reach tools and data.

deepDives.title: NIST Agent Standards Initiative hub
deepDives.why: Official hub for US standards work on agent security, identity and interoperability.

deepDives.title: Epoch AI: OSWorld 2.0
deepDives.why: A live measure of how well agents complete long computer tasks.

deepDives.title: Stanford HAI: AI Index
deepDives.why: Annual independent data on AI adoption, investment and measured business impact.

deepDives.title: OECD AI Incidents and Hazards Monitor: agent data leaks
deepDives.why: Entry point to a public database of AI incidents, including agent data leaks.
